first.rationale: The two declining metrics are causally linked: onboarding completion (-4%) sits upstream of activation (-6%), so fixing completion is the higher-leverage single move and may recover part of the activation gap as a second-order effect. memory_86 directly supports shortening onboarding (completion, time-to-value, early adoption across self-serve), and memory_31 gives converging evidence that reducing friction early lifts SMB activation durably. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records real acquisition and revenue lift but a material 30-day retention hit and an explicit warning not to generalize it, which conflicts with the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective. referral_incentive (memory_57) was validated in established customers and does nothing for the two metrics that are actually degrading; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) targets a segment that is not the source of the decline. I spend verification on memory_86 because my chosen action rests on it, and on memory_91 because activation_messaging is the strongest alternative and the larger raw decline is in activation \ing a strong original record there could flip my choice. Both memories are consolidated summaries whose original records may have been narrower in scope, shorter in horizon, or measured on different populations than my current one; the summaries also report proximal metrics (completion, engagement, first meaningful action) rather than retained qualified revenue, so a lift there is not yet evidence of the outcome I am optimizing for. Downstream risk to flag: shortening onboarding can strip steps that qualify or educate accounts, inflating completion and activation counts while admitting lower-intent accounts \ the same failure shape as memory_73, where a proximal win masked retention damage. I will therefore instrument the test with 30-day retention and qualified-revenue-per-cohort as pre-registered guardrails, not just completion rate, and treat any completion lift unaccompanied by retained revenue as a null or negative result.

final.rationale: Verification changed my decision. memory_86 turned out to be a lossy consolidation: the source record (exp_86) shows completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days, but also 60-day churn +9% concentrated in complex-workspace accounts, with an explicit instruction not to roll out there. The inherited summary had dropped the harm and the scope restriction entirely, which is exactly the failure pattern memory_73 warns about \ a proximal win (completion) masking retained-revenue damage. Running simplify_onboarding as the summary described would have been a net-negative move against a sustainable qualified-revenue objective. exp_91, by contrast, verified clean and stronger than its summary: week-one engagement +11%, activation +6%, and 30-day retention +1%. It is the only candidate with a positive retention signal rather than a neutral or negative one, and it targets activation, which is the larger of the two declines (-6% QoQ) and the metric closer to realized value. I am not choosing promotional_pricing: memory_73's retention damage makes it a way to buy the competitor's price-sensitive churn at a loss, and matching aggressive entry pricing is a poor response to a value problem. referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist address neither declining metric. Preserved uncertainty: exp_91 is a single prior study, and I do not know whether it ran under the same competitive pressure or cohort mix as today \ a +6% activation lift measured in a calmer quarter may not fully close a -6% decline driven partly by competitor-induced mix shift toward lower-intent accounts. The onboarding completion gap (-4%) also remains unaddressed and is upstream of activation, so messaging may only partially recover it; the correct follow-up is a complex-workspace-excluded onboarding test, not the broad version memory_86 implied. Downstream risk to flag: activation messaging can inflate 'first meaningful action' counts by nudging accounts through a tracked event without real adoption, so I will pre-register 30-day retention and qualified-revenue-per-cohort as guardrails alongside activation rate, segment results by workspace complexity to catch heterogeneous effects like the one exp_86 hid, and treat an activation lift without retained revenue as null. I am also writing the corrected scope restriction back into memory_86 so the next agent does not inherit the sanitized version.
